plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling fields of silvery-green shrubs erupt in spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers. They hum with bees and scent the warm summer air with a sweet, herbal perfume.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, peaking in July
plants.location: Provence and the French Alps, France
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: South Africa's national flower is a huge, bowl-shaped bloom up to 30 cm across. It has a crown of stiff, silky-tipped bracts in shades of pink and cream, and it stands out against the winter fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to October (late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Fynbos regions of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The genus is named after the Greek sea god Proteus, who could change shape. The name nods to how varied proteas are.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, goblet-shaped blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. The petals open at dawn in pink and white and give off a soft, sweet fragrance over still summer ponds.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to August in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate summer
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across temperate and subtropical Asia
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic texture that makes water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt away. Scientists call this the 'lotus effect' and have copied it in self-cleaning materials.
